events.label: founding
events.text: Government authorizes creation of NYRBA do Brasil subsidiary.

evidence.quote: The creation of this subsidiary was authorized on October 15 , 1929

events.label: founding
events.text: Began operations as NYRBA do Brasil S.A., subsidiary of NYRBA.

evidence.quote: Panair do Brasil began operations on October 22 , 1929 , as NYRBA do Brasil S.A.

events.label: service launch
events.text: First flight inaugurated, Rio de Janeiro to Buenos Aires.

evidence.quote: The first flight took off from the Calabouço Airport
in Rio de Janeiro to Buenos Aires with intermediate stops on December 23 , 1929

events.label: service launch
events.text: Rio de Janeiro to Fortaleza service started with intermediate stops.

evidence.quote: in January 1930 it started flying between Rio de Janeiro and Fortaleza

events.label: authorization
events.text: Operations authorized throughout Brazilian territory.

evidence.quote: on January 24 , 1930 its operations were authorized in all Brazilian territory

events.label: cargo operation
events.text: First cargo operation Buenos Aires to Miami, joint venture with NYRBA, lasted to 25 Feb.

evidence.quote: took place between February 19 and 25 , 1930

events.text: NYRBA, parent of the subsidiary, sold to Pan American.

evidence.quote: On April 30 , 1930 NYRBA was sold to Pan American

events.text: New owner renamed NYRBA do Brasil as Panair do Brasil.

evidence.quote: on November 21 , 1930 the new owner of the subsidiary renamed NYRBA do Brasil as Panair do Brasil

events.label: service launch
events.text: Regular passenger services began, Belém to Rio de Janeiro.

evidence.quote: Regular passenger services began on March 2 , 1931 with a flight between Belém and Rio de Janeiro

events.label: service launch
events.text: Services to Brazil's interior started, competing with Syndicato Condor.

evidence.quote: Starting in 1933 , Panair do Brasil , competing with Syndicato Condor established services to the interior of Brazil

events.text: Opened dedicated headquarters at Santos Dumont Airport, Rio de Janeiro.

evidence.quote: In 1937 Panair opened its own dedicated headquarters at Santos Dumont Airport in Rio de Janeiro

events.label: fleet acquisition
events.text: Received its first land planes, a Lockheed Model 10 Electra.

evidence.quote: In October 1937 Panair received its first land planes , a Lockheed Model 10 Electra

events.text: Decree-Law 3.462 authorizes Panair to build and maintain several airports.

evidence.quote: by the Federal Decree-Law 3.462 of June 25 , 1941 , Panair was authorized to build , enhance and maintain the airports

events.text: Pan American sold a large portion of its shares to Brazilian capital.

evidence.quote: until 1942 , when the latter sold a big portion of shares to Brazilian capital

events.text: Authorized to fly to all South American countries.

evidence.quote: That same year Panair was authorized to fly to all South American countries

events.label: service launch
events.text: First overnight service in Brazil, Rio to Belém, with intermediate stops.

evidence.quote: starting on September 2 , 1943 the first overnight service in Brazil : Rio/Belém with intermediate stops

events.text: Pan American's shareholding reduced to 58%.

evidence.quote: On December 7 , 1943 the participation of Pan American was further reduced to 58%

events.text: Majority of shares (52%) held by Brazilian nationals.

evidence.quote: In 1946 , the majority of its shares - 52% - was in the hands of Brazilian nationals

events.label: fleet acquisition
events.text: Received its first Lockheed 049 Constellation.

evidence.quote: In March 1946 Panair received its first Lockheed 049 Constellation

events.label: service launch
events.text: First flight with its Lockheed Constellation, from Rio de Janeiro to Recife, Dakar, Lisbon, Paris and London.

evidence.quote: The first flight took off on April 27 , 1946 from Rio de Janeiro to Recife , Dakar , Lisbon , Paris and London

events.label: route launch
events.text: Services extended to Cairo and Istanbul.

evidence.quote: In 1947 services were extended to Cairo and Istanbul

events.label: route launch
events.text: Services to Zurich and Frankfurt started.

evidence.quote: in 1948 to Zurich and Frankfurt

events.label: route launch
events.text: Services to Montevideo and Buenos Aires began.

evidence.quote: The same year , services to Montevideo and Buenos Aires began

events.label: route launch
events.text: Services to Santiago de Chile, Lima and Beirut added.

evidence.quote: Santiago de Chile , Lima and Beirut were added in 1950

events.label: aircraft order
events.text: Ordered 4 de Havilland Comet 2 aircraft, with option for 2 Comet 3.

evidence.quote: In 1953 Panair placed an order for 4 de Havilland Comet 2

events.label: order cancellation
events.text: Comet orders cancelled due to flaws in original design.

evidence.quote: Those orders were canceled in 1954 due to flaws on the planes original design

events.label: route launch
events.text: Services to Hamburg and Düsseldorf added.

evidence.quote: and Hamburg and Düsseldorf in 1954

events.label: aircraft purchase
events.text: Bought 4 Douglas DC-7C using unused Comet order funds.

evidence.quote: In 1955 the unused funds of the Comet order were used to purchase 4 Douglas DC-7C

events.label: agreement
events.text: Agreement with Lóide Aéreo Nacional to avoid harmful competition begins.

evidence.quote: between 1956 and 1958 Panair and Lóide Aéreo Nacional maintained an agreement to avoid harmful competition

events.label: aircraft delivery
events.text: First of the Douglas DC-7C aircraft arrived.

evidence.quote: The first arrived in 1957

events.label: agreement
events.text: Agreement with Lóide Aéreo Nacional ends.

evidence.quote: between 1956 and 1958 Panair and Lóide Aéreo Nacional maintained an agreement to avoid harmful competition

events.label: joint service
events.text: Voo da amizade joint service with TAP begins, running to 1965.

evidence.quote: Between November 30 , 1960 and 1965 Panair operated with TAP-Transportes Aéreos Portugueses the Voo da amizade

events.label: route launch
events.text: Started operating Douglas DC-8-33 jets to Europe.

evidence.quote: In 1961 , Panair started operating the Douglas DC-8-33 to Europe

events.label: aircraft purchase
events.text: Purchased 4 Sud Aviation Caravelle aircraft.

evidence.quote: In 1961 Panair purchased 4 Sud Aviation Caravelle

events.text: Last block of shares held by Pan Am sold.

evidence.quote: The last lot of shares in the hands of Pan Am was sold in 1961

events.label: aircraft entry into service
events.text: Caravelle jets entered service on domestic trunk and South American routes.

evidence.quote: which entered into service in 1962 , operating on domestic trunk routes
In 1962 , Panair incorporated SUD SE-210 Caravelle 6-R jet aircraft

events.label: joint service
events.text: Voo da amizade joint service with TAP ended

evidence.quote: Between November 30 , 1960 and 1965 Panair operated with TAP-Transportes Aéreos Portugueses the Voo da amizade

events.label: shutdown
events.text: Operations forcibly ceased under military government order.

evidence.quote: It ceased operations in 1965
forced to cease operations abruptly on February 10 , 1965

events.text: Route concessions and aircraft transferred to Varig and Cruzeiro do Sul.

evidence.quote: allotted its international route concessions to Varig and domestic to Cruzeiro do Sul
forced to cease operations abruptly on February 10 , 1965

events.label: bankruptcy
events.text: Court declared Panair officially bankrupt under military pressure.

evidence.quote: declared Panair officially bankrupt on February 15 , 1965

events.label: court ruling
events.text: Supreme Federal Court acknowledged regular operation; government ordered to pay reparations.

evidence.quote: On December 14 , 1984 , the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court acknowledged that the airline had operated within regular technical and financial parameters

events.label: bankruptcy suspension
events.text: Forced bankruptcy suspended.

evidence.quote: The forced bankruptcy was suspended on May 5 , 1995

events.label: concession revocation
events.text: Air Command revoked Panair's route and schedule concessions.

evidence.quote: On August 27 , 2009 , after a 44-year delay , the Air Command of the Brazilian Ministry of Defence revoked Panairs route

undated_mentions: 1940s: continually opened new domestic services; extensive domestic network
ONeill attempted to purchase ETA (Empresa de Transporte Aéreo); sale aborted
ONeill decided to create his own Brazilian subsidiary in partnership with NYRBA
Brazilian government granted concession to operate services to Europe (after 1946 share change)
Flights to Madrid and Rome inaugurated
Operational pool formed with Aerolíneas Argentinas, Alitalia and Lufthansa
First international airline to land at London Heathrow Airport
Filed for bankruptcy protection while lawyers debated the issue in Court
